# Probook Raises $40M in Seed and Series A Financing

 By FinSMEs 

June 23, 2026

Probook founders Ben Cervantez, George Eliadis and Lewis Zhang.

Probook, a New York City-based developer of an AI-powered operating system for home service businesses, raised $40m in a combined Seed and Series A financing.

The round comprised a $34m Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and a $6m seed round led by Sequoia Capital, with Sequoia also participating in the Series A tranche.

The company intends to use the funds to scale its go-to-market operations to meet surging demand, expand its software engineering capabilities, and grow its customer success teams to manage national deployments.

Led by Co-founders George Eliadis (CEO), Ben Cervantez, and Lewis Zhang, Probook develops a unified AI operating system built around a centralized dispatch engine that consolidates customer intake, automated data cleaning, SMS text messaging threads, and outbound scheduling into a single context layer.

The company has expanded its platform footprint to manage hundreds of service locations nationwide, automating unassisted bookings for major private equity-backed home service brands—including TurnPoint Services, Master Trades Group, Del-Air, Peterman Brothers, and Sila Services.

# Probook Raises $40M from a16z and Sequoia to Build the Trades' AI Operating System Around Dispatch
...
The home-services startup — serving HVAC, plumbing and electrical shops — raised a $6M seed led by Sequoia and a $34M Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz, a rare co-sign from two firms that seldom share a cap table. Founded by a 24-year-old who grew up pressure-washing houses, Probook is betting the trades' back office consolidates into one platform built around the dispatch board.

 HP Hugo Pegley Editor & Founder 

 

Probook has raised $40 million to become what it calls the AI operating system for home services — the HVAC, plumbing and electrical shops that run on a dispatch board. The money came in two parts: a $6 million seed led by Sequoia Capital and a $34 million Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz, with Sequoia participating, according to the company and Fortune, which first reported the round.
...
The detail that will catch an investor’s eye is the cap table. a16z and Sequoia rarely lead into the same company; when they do, it usually means both believe they are looking at a category winner. Probook’s General Partner backers — David Haber at a16z and Konstantine Buhler at Sequoia — are betting on a market most of venture has historically ignored: the back office of the skilled trades.
